\[ \text{Distance per time step} = 0.70 \times \frac{1}{30} = \frac{0.70}{30} \approx 0.0233 \text{ image widths} \]

In 40 time steps, the total distance moved is:

\[ \text{Total distance} = 0.0233 \times 40 \approx 0.932 \text{ image widths} \]

Since the pink rectangle starts at the left edge of the image (position 0), after 40 time steps, it will be at approximately position 0.932. Given the discrete nature of the image, we can consider it to be at position 1 (since it moves slightly more than 1 pixel to the right).

The pink rectangle is 1 unit wide, so it will cover columns 1 to 2 (0-based indexing, columns 1 and 2).

Now, we need to create a 32x32 binary grid where the pink rectangle covers columns 1 and 2 in the row where it is located. Since the pink rectangle is only 1 row high (as it is a rectangle with height 1), it will cover only one row.

The pink rectangle is located in the bottom row of the image (row 31 in 0-based indexing).

Thus, the grid will have '1's in columns 1 and 2 of row 31, and '0's everywhere else.
